pysnap.terminal package¶

Terminal interface components for PySnap.

Submodules¶

pysnap.terminal.clipboard module¶

Read the host clipboard for the Ctrl-] v paste of pysnap connect.

The clipboard is read only when the user asks for it. Copying and the usual paste are left to the terminal of the user; this paste helps where the terminal offers none from the keyboard, such as the Windows console without its Ctrl key shortcuts.

  • Windows: the Win32 clipboard API through ctypes, no external program;

  • macOS: pbpaste;

  • Linux and other systems: wl-paste under Wayland, then xclip or xsel for the X11 clipboard.

pysnap.terminal.emulator module¶

Terminal emulation utilities built on top of pyte.

class pysnap.terminal.emulator.SequenceFilter[source]¶

Bases: object

Remove control sequences pyte cannot handle before it parses them.

pyte 0.8 fails on some sequences that current programs send, for example editors such as Vim with an xterm TERM:

  • private CSI sequences other than DEC modes, such as ESC [ ? 4 m, raise TypeError;

  • >, = and < prefixes are ignored, so ESC [ > 4 ; 2 m switches on underline;

  • intermediate bytes (ESC [ 0 % m) and colon sub-parameters (ESC [ 3 8 : 2 : : 1 : 2 : 3 m) end the sequence early and the rest is drawn as text;

  • the payload of DCS, SOS, PM and APC strings is drawn as text.

The filter keeps the sequences pyte handles, rewrites colon SGR parameters to the semicolon form and drops the rest, together with all control strings (including OSC: window titles are not used). Its state survives chunk boundaries, so a sequence split between two reads is handled like a whole one.

feed(data)[source]¶

Return the bytes of data that pyte may parse.

Parameters:

data (bytes) – Raw guest output.

Returns:

Filtered output; parts of an unfinished sequence are kept until the next call.

Return type:

bytes

class pysnap.terminal.emulator.ScrollRegionMixin[source]¶

Bases: object

Add the CSI S and T scroll commands that pyte 0.8 lacks.

Programs such as nano scroll their editing area with them when the terminal is an xterm. The scroll happens inside the scrolling margins and does not move the cursor; it reuses index and reverse_index so that screens which track lines leaving the screen see them as usual.

class pysnap.terminal.emulator.AlternateScreenMixin[source]¶

Bases: object

Give a pyte history screen the xterm alternate screen.

Full-screen programs such as vim, nano and less switch to the alternate screen and back when they exit, so the shell screen reappears as it was. Lines scrolled on the alternate screen do not enter the history, as in xterm. pyte 0.8 has no alternate screen: it ignores these modes.

feed(data)[source]¶

Feed new bytes into the terminal parser.

Parsing while the local viewport is scrolled back would write into the manually rotated history buffers and lose lines, so the view first returns to the live bottom. This mirrors the common jump-to-bottom-on-output behavior of desktop terminals.

Control sequences pyte cannot handle are filtered first (see SequenceFilter).

Parameters:

data (bytes) – Raw bytes read from the guest connection.

Return type:

None

pysnap.terminal.keymap.paste_to_bytes(text, *, bracketed)[source]¶

Return pasted text as the bytes a terminal sends for it.

Line breaks of any system (CR LF, LF) become CR, the Enter key of a terminal, so a text copied on Windows does not give empty lines. When the guest asked for bracketed paste (ESC [ ? 2004 h, as bash and vim do), the text is put between ESC [ 200 ~ and ESC [ 201 ~; markers inside the text are removed, so that it cannot end the paste early.

Parameters:

  • text (str) – Pasted text.

  • bracketed (bool) – Whether the guest enabled bracketed paste.

Returns:

UTF-8 bytes for the guest.

Return type:

bytes

pysnap.terminal.protocol module¶

Helpers for terminal control-sequence handling over serial TCP.

class pysnap.terminal.protocol.TerminalQueryResponder(_buffer=<factory>)[source]¶

Bases: object

Recognize terminal queries and synthesize compatible replies.

Raw serial consoles do not provide a PTY-style SIGWINCH channel into the guest system. PySnap therefore acts like a small terminal emulator and replies to xterm-compatible size queries that guest-side tools may emit.

Parameters:

_buffer (bytearray)

collect_responses(data, *, emulator, columns, lines)[source]¶

Return terminal replies implied by one incoming byte chunk.

Parameters:

  • data (bytes) – Newly received bytes from the guest.

  • emulator (TerminalEmulator) – Emulator holding the current cursor position.

  • columns (int) – Current visible terminal width.

  • lines (int) – Current visible terminal height.

Returns:

Zero or more response payloads to send back to the guest.

Return type:

list[bytes]

pysnap.terminal.transport.serial_connection_probe(host, port, timeout=30.0, retry_delay=0.25)[source]¶

Open a short-lived serial TCP connection for automated checks.

The probe writes one newline to verify that the transport accepts client output and then keeps the connection open for the caller-managed context.

Parameters:

  • port (int) – Target TCP port.
